chunks: I advise you, O creatures of Allah,

to have fear of Allah, which is the provision and with it is the return. The provision is that which reaches its destination and the return is that which succeeds. The best caller has called to it, and the best listener has listened to it. So the caller has proclaimed and the listener has succeeded.

key_terms.أَسْمَعُ دَاع: The most hearing caller, referring to one who effectively conveys the message
key_terms.الزَّاد: Provision, metaphorically referring to spiritual deeds prepared for the afterlife
key_terms.الْمَعَاذ: The means of return or refuge, indicating the successful journey back to God
key_terms.تَقْوَى: God-consciousness or piety, the central theme of the exhortation
key_terms.خَيْرُ وَاع: The best listener, referring to one who attentively receives and preserves the message

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Taqwa as a provision for the Hereafter in Shia sermons?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) employs the metaphor of 'Zad' (provision) and 'Ma'adh' (safe return) to frame Taqwa not merely as a virtue but as the essential logistical preparation for the existential journey of life, a concept deeply rooted in Shia eschatological thought. This passage underscores the reciprocal dynamic between the preacher and the listener, emphasizing that spiritual success depends on both effective dissemination and faithful internalization of divine guidance.

en.sayed-ali-raza: [Enjoining people to Piety :] O creatures of Allāh ! I advise you

to have fear of Allah which is the provision (for next world) and with it is (your) return. The provision would take you (to your destination) and the return would be successful. The best one, who is able to make people listen has called towards it and the best listener has listened to it. So the caller has proclaimed and the listener has listened and preserved.
